text.p: LG&E Energy Corp Friday reported lower first quarter profits citing natural gas volatility and saying it expects earnings for the year will exceed 1996's $1.57 per share.
First quarter earnings of $0.32 cents per share were down from a restated $0.41 per share in 1996's first quarter. Earnings in that period were reported as $0.33 per share.

The company said earnings were restrained by mild winter weather, the effect of the devastating March flood in the Louisville area and moderate natural gas prices, which reduced margins in the company's gas trading business.
For the first three months of the year, the company generated net income of $21.2 million compared with $27.1 million in the same period in 1996.
It noted 1996 earnings were restated at year end to reflect LG&E's conversion to the mark-to-market method of accounting for its marketing businesses.

Revenues increased 49 percent to $1.3 billion, compared with $875 million during the same period last year. This increase reflects continued sales growth in the company's energy marketing business, it said.

Although first quarter earnings were lower than in the comparable period in 1996, "the company expects that earnings for the full year 1997 will exceed those of 1996, assuming normal weather during the remainder of the year."
Spokesman Steve Wilson said LG&E expects 1997 earnings to exceed 1996 net income of $1.57 per share.
The company earned $1.83 per share before special items in 1996, he noted.
In the 12 months ended March 31, LG&E reported, it had net income per share of $1.48 compared to $1.36 a year earlier.
The First Call consensus estimate for the first quarter was $0.34 per share and $1.68 for all of 1997.
Louisville Gas and Electric Co, the company's regulated utility, contributed $0.34 per share to earnings, equal to earnings reported for the first three months of 1996.

LG&E said the utility's results reflect lower operation and maintenance expenses despite the costs incurred as a result of severe flooding in the Louisville area. Earnings were limited by warm weather during the quarter.
The non-utility businesses contributed $0.03 in the latest quarter, compared with $0.16 per share a year earlier.
The independent power generation and power marketing operations were profitable during the first quarter, while natural gas marketing showed a loss, Wilson said.

The company's expectations of better than year earlier results in the final three quarters of 1997 are based on its belief the energy marketing unit will make greater contributions to earnings, he said.
During the quarter, power marketing sales volumes exceeded 10 million megawatthours, up 66 percent from the fourth quarter of 1996. Sales volumes for all of 1996 totaled 17 million megawatt hours.
Mild weather throughout much of the country, coupled with low price volatility in gas markets, however, lowered profit margins in the gas marketing business, the company said.

It noted this compared to the strong performance at the gas marketing unit a year earlier due to extreme fluctuations in weather during the period and extraordinarily volatile prices. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
